subject: axolotl
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.
reasoning:
I'm planning a chibi axolotl design with a big head, short body, stubby legs, a finned tail, and three frilly gill stalks on each side, keeping proportions cute and compact at roughly 0.25-0.3 meters while being mindful of using the API correctly.

Setting up the skeleton structure...

Defining tail sweep geometry...

Tail tube tapers with a rounded cap. For the head I'm using a squashed, scaled sphere positioned forward for a chibi look, colored in leucistic axolotl pink with countershaded belly tones and mottled freckles, sized wider than the body for that cute proportion.

I'm checking vertical clearance so the head and body bottoms sit just above the floor, then planning the face: a decal with a smile curve, nostrils, and cheek blush, plus small bead-like eyes placed symmetrically near the top-front of the head using local coordinates.

I'm working out the exact eye-sphere placement by solving for where the head ellipsoid surface sits at a given x/z offset, then adding black spheres with tiny white highlight spheres for eyes, and blush circles via decal alongside the smile and nostrils.

I'm placing a face decal on the front of the head using the surface math I just worked out, then adding a small squashed-sphere jaw piece tucked mostly inside the head so only a sliver shows at the bottom front.

Now I'm designing gill stalks on each side of the head's back, built as swept bezier tubes in deep pink, with tapering frond spikes arranged along each stalk perpendicular to the tangent direction.

Still working out frond geometry...

Front legs run from shoulder root through a mid joint to the foot, using a three-point curve with a pink capsule sweep tapering toward the tip. For the feet, I'll fan out small capsule toes forward from the foot point to suggest claws.

Hind legs mirror this with their own root-to-tip chain positioned further back and lower, with toes angled backward. Both leg chains get swept with tapering radii for a smooth capsule shape, and I'm defining the body radius as a function along its path, varying ellipse width and height to create the bulging torso shape from tail to chest.

Working out the bottom clearance and tail taper so the body and tail radii blend smoothly where they overlap near the hips, then moving on to define the skin color using a mottled pink countershading pattern.

I'm layering spots and a belly countershade over the base skin texture, then setting gill coloring and considering shiny eye decals as an alternative to geometric eyes.

For the eyes, I'm thinking through projecting a flat circular decal onto the head using the surface normal at the eye location on the ellipsoid, computing the approximate normal vector from the body's radii to orient the decal correctly rather than wrapping a texture around a separate sphere.

Adding blush decals with a radial gradient, placing a decal call for the face with position, direction and size, and sketching the smile path in the face SVG.

Now I'm writing the gill-building function that sweeps a bezier curve into a thin tube shape and samples points along it to compute tangent and perpendicular vectors for placing fronds.

I'll add a small bright sphere tip to each spike for visual polish, and figure the spike count works out fine across all stalks. For the head, I'll use a scaled low-poly sphere with skin color, keeping it smooth for cleaner paint coverage, and skip extra crest detail. For the feet, I need to pull toe positions from the leg chain's tip joint location.

Legs get capsule segments using the final joint in each chain, with front legs rooted at the spine and hind legs at the hips, named per side (hip/knee/foot). Toes fan out directionally in the xz-plane, pointing forward for front feet and backward for hind feet, with small radius and offset tip positions.

That settles the structure -- time to write it out.
